solver.algorithm: Discounted CFR (α = 1.5, β = 0.5, γ = 3), alternating updates, exact best-response exploitability

approximations: Turn and river subgames start from the scenario's preflop ranges; the synthetic flop/turn line that sets pot and stacks does not narrow them.
Bet trees are deliberately lean (two bet sizes, one raise size, limited raises), so the equilibrium is for that abstraction.
Solves stop near the target exploitability, so EV differences below ~0.25% of the pot are treated as ties.
Spots where every action is within 2% of the pot of each other are skipped as trivial.
EV loss is measured against a GTO opponent, not against the leaks of a real one.

variants.summary: Default: full state with derived facts (made hand, draws, pot odds, SPR) + one choice question
Raw facts only (cards, positions, pot/stacks/to-call, history, actions); no derived facts
v2 + hero equity and made-hand percentile vs villain's preflop range (Monte-Carlo), equity vs needed
eq, but equity vs villain's range narrowed by its actions (strength heuristic, no solver data)
v2 state; criteria rewritten as concise GTO theory (value/bluff/bluff-catch, MDF, polarisation)
v2 state; 3 independently answered choice questions (v2 / coach / solver phrasing), probabilities averaged
v2 state; one noul per action ('is <action> the highest-EV action?'), P(true) normalised
eqrange + exact nut ranking (holdings that beat hero now) + value-extraction guidance for strong hands
v2 + short-stack preflop guidance (≤25bb: limp/call, fold or shove; small raises rarely best)

criteria.allin: All-in for 87.1 bb (a raise of 97% of the pot after calling): the hero commits the whole remaining stack, making the pot 135 bb; the villain can only call or fold. Right with the very strongest hands, or as a bluff when the villain folds often enough.
criteria.call: Call 20.5 bb: the hero matches the villain's bet, making the pot 68.5 bb. The hero needs at least 30% equity against the villain's betting range to break even. The next board card is then dealt. Right when the hero beats enough of the villain's bluffs and thin value bets, but raising would not earn more.
criteria.fold: Fold: the hero gives up the hand, puts in no more chips and forfeits the 47.9 bb pot. Right when the hero's hand wins too rarely against the villain's betting range to justify paying 20.5 bb (it needs 30% equity).

action.instructions: You are advising the hero, the player whose turn it is, in the heads-up No-Limit Texas Hold'em spot described in the state. Pick the single legal action that maximises the hero's expected value against a strong, balanced, game-theory-optimal (GTO) opponent who cannot see the hero's cards. Weigh the hero's exact hand against the villain's likely range given the betting so far, blockers, pot odds, the stack-to-pot ratio and position. Bet and raise sizes are fixed; choose only among the listed actions.
